description:
After bd:JMAP-ic0j.71 added `UTCDate::to_epoch_seconds()` to `jmap-types` (foundation), `jmap-mail-server` still carries its own private `rfc3339_to_epoch_secs` / `try_rfc3339_to_epoch_secs` parser at `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:2111-2189`. That helper accepts RFC 3339 with offset (`+HH:MM` / `-HH:MM`) AND the `Z` suffix, so it's a SUPERSET of `UTCDate::to_epoch_seconds`, which is strictly RFC 8620 §1.4 (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).

Migration targets in jmap-mail-server:

- `memory.rs:203`: `.map(rfc3339_to_epoch_secs)` on `Email.received_at` — `received_at` is a `UTCDate` field (RFC 8621 §4.1), so this is a clean swap.
- `memory.rs:923-924`: `rfc3339_to_epoch_secs` on `received_at` for sort comparison — same.
- `memory.rs:2259, 2267`: `rfc3339_to_epoch_secs(email.received_at.as_ref())` — same.

NOT a migration target:
- `memory.rs:2260, 2268`: `try_rfc3339_to_epoch_secs` on filter `before` / `after` which are bare strings that MIGHT carry offsets. Keep the offset-aware helper here, OR add a separate `Date::to_epoch_seconds` to `jmap-types` (RFC 8620 §1.4 Date type allows non-UTC offsets) and migrate to that. Decide as part of this work.

Acceptance:
- Mail-server uses `received_at.to_epoch_seconds()?` directly where the input is typed as `UTCDate`.
- Private helper retained only for the cases where the input is genuinely RFC 3339 with offset.
- `cargo test -p jmap-mail-server` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p jmap-mail-server -- -D warnings` passes.

Out of scope for bd:JMAP-ic0j.71 (which is calendars-server only). Filed under the same parent epic because the cookie-cutter sibling pattern means whatever shape mail-server settles on becomes the canonical for other extension siblings.
title: Migrate jmap-mail-server::memory::rfc3339_to_epoch_secs to jmap-types::UTCDate::to_epoch_seconds where applicable
